title: The Future of Proactive AI Systems

slides.title: At 3:12 AM It Finished
slides.headline: My assistant completed work while I was asleep.
bullets: At 3:12 AM the AI finished work with nobody online.
One WhatsApp command triggered the full workflow.
The result arrived as completed artifacts, not a chat reply.
slides.notes: Open with the overnight proof moment.

slides.title: Reactive AI Waits For Prompts
slides.headline: Most assistants answer once and disappear.
bullets: Most AI assistants today are still reactive.
They wait for prompts, answer questions, then vanish.
That is not how useful systems behave.
slides.notes: Frame the core problem the architecture solves.

slides.title: Reliable Systems Run Continuously
slides.headline: Useful infrastructure does not wait to be asked.
bullets: Email servers do not wait for prompts.
Build pipelines do not wait for prompts.
Monitoring systems do not wait for prompts.
slides.notes: Use familiar infra analogies to reset expectations.

slides.title: Architecture Beats Bigger Models
slides.headline: The shift is system design, not model size.
bullets: The shift is not about bigger models.
Instead of building a chatbot, we built an assistant system.
Proactive behavior comes from architecture.
slides.notes: Emphasize why stack design matters more than model swaps.

slides.title: Three Layers Handle The Work
slides.headline: OpenClaw, Sherbyte, and workers split responsibility.
bullets: OpenClaw handles channels, tools, orchestration.
Sherbyte manages messages, context, and heartbeat checks.
Background workers execute tasks and emit receipts.

slides.title: OpenClaw Is Runtime Fabric
slides.headline: OpenClaw is the orchestration backbone.
bullets: It is responsible for channels, tools, and orchestration.
It routes task intake and execution across components.
It provides the runtime substrate for agent workflows.
slides.notes: Zoom into layer one with concrete scope.

slides.title: Sherbyte Is The Human Bridge
slides.headline: Sherbyte keeps the human loop coherent.
bullets: It manages messages and context continuity.
Heartbeat checks maintain escalation visibility.
It turns backend progress into human-readable updates.

slides.title: Workers Execute Headless Jobs
slides.headline: Background workers do the heavy lifting autonomously.
bullets: They read tasks from a durable queue.
They perform work and generate artifacts.
They emit execution receipts and notifications.
slides.notes: Explain why execution is separated from chat.

slides.title: Durable Queue Drives Lifecycle
slides.headline: Every task moves through explicit, auditable states.
bullets: Lifecycle: pending -> in_progress -> done/failed.
Dependencies use depends_on for deterministic ordering.
Retries and scheduling are controlled via run_after.
slides.notes: Show reliability through explicit state transitions.

slides.title: Resilience Without Hidden State
slides.headline: Recovery works because queue state is the truth.
bullets: If a worker crashes, the next cycle recovers stale locks.
No hidden state and no fragile memory tricks.
Deterministic progress replaces guesswork.
slides.notes: Highlight crash recovery and idempotent reruns.

slides.title: Full Loop In One Line
slides.headline: Human input flows through a closed execution loop.
bullets: Human (WhatsApp) -> Sherbyte -> OpenClaw Runtime
OpenClaw Runtime -> Durable Task Queue
Task Queue -> Background Worker -> Artifacts + Notifications
slides.notes: Present the end-to-end architecture text diagram.

slides.title: A Message Becomes A Job
slides.headline: !task converts intent into executable work.
bullets: A WhatsApp command becomes a queue item.
The worker executes asynchronously in the background.
Results return as artifacts plus notifications.

slides.title: Overnight Run Across 18 Sources
slides.headline: One run produced a complete research brief autonomously.
bullets: The system scraped 18 sources overnight.
It generated a structured research brief.
It saved artifacts, emitted receipts, and delivered results back to WhatsApp.
slides.notes: Use this as proof of practical throughput.

slides.title: Four Lessons From Building
slides.headline: Reliability comes from discipline, not vibes.
bullets: Separate interaction from execution.
Treat failure as first-class with retries, dedup, escalation.
Produce receipts for everything.
Make tasks idempotent so reruns are safe.

slides.title: From Chatbot To Agent OS
slides.headline: This is an operating system for agents.
bullets: The architecture resembles a distributed system runtime.
Future assistants are coordinated systems, not single chats.
Queues, workers, artifacts, and oversight enable proactive AI.
slides.notes: Close with the reframe and future direction.
